page.layout: One printed page, running head and page number at top. One text column with a marginal note in the left margin at the second paragraph. Below a rule: a chapter heading (CAP. XVII. with an italic title, centred), then the opening paragraph of the chapter with a large initial T.

p.i: præparationem alterius maxillæ, in corde faciendam. Vt Dominus potius misericorditer perferendam alterius infirmitatem indicet, quam alieno supplicio suam mitigandam: Neque tamen hic ea vindicta prohibetur, quæ ad correctionem valet. Ipsa enim pertinet ad misericordiam, nec impedit illud propositum, quo quisque paratus est ab eo, quem correctum esse vult, plura perferre.
Et alibi: quæri autem potest, quid sit dextera maxilla. Sed cum facies sit, quâ quisque cognoscitur, in faciem cædi, secundum Apostolum est, contemni, despici.

main_text.head: CAP. XVII. An si provocans interfecerit provocatum justa defensionis beneficio usus esse censeatur, aut vice versâ?
main_text.p: Turbator pacis publicæ aliquem in via est aggres-sus[?]

page.notes: The drop-cap T is joined to "urbator" as "Turbator". The last word is split at the line end as "aggres-" and "sus"; the second part is set so that it reads like "fus" on the scan and is marked [?]. No catchword, signature or other furniture is printed at the foot. A faint mark at the bottom right is a digitiser's or scanner artefact and is left out.
